answer: Each agent must post a slashable stake before it earns votes or reputation. To flood the network with a thousand fake identities, an attacker must lock a thousand separate deposits, and any detected lie burns the whole bond, so the cost grows linearly with every sybil while honest agents reclaim their stake. Trust is carved from basalt: the kernel of each identity is expensive to cut, and a forged one slips off the ledge and shatters.
